region.name: Southwestern Amazon (Rondônia)
region.setting: Tropical rainforest with extensive land clearing since the 1980s. The box covers the Brazilian state of Rondônia and neighbouring parts of Bolivia and of other Brazilian states.

variable.name: Root-zone soil wetness
variable.definition: How full of water the top meter of soil is: 0 is completely dry, 1 is saturated.

verdict.title: Significant falling trend that holds across date ranges
verdict.text: Over 1981-2025 the series changed by -0.0227 fraction (0-1) per decade. Both significance tests agree after allowing for month-to-month persistence, and 99% of all date windows of 15+ years point the same way.

crosscheck.label: No second dataset checked
crosscheck.text: This result has not been compared with an independent dataset. It describes this dataset; whether another record would show the same is not known.

known_issue.title: Known data issue: this soil wetness is driven by rainfall that shifts in 2005

sources.label: Reichle et al. (2017), Land Surface Precipitation in MERRA-2, J. Climate 30(5), 1643–1664
Reichle (2023), The Land Surface in Earth System Reanalysis, slide 12 (NASA NTRS 20230012995)

known_issue.credit: Found by the team's scientific validation review (SCIENTIFIC_VALIDATION.md).
known_issue.text: MERRA-2 computes soil wetness from its gauge-corrected rainfall. In this box that rainfall drops against an independent record in 2005 for a documented data reason (open Precipitation for this region), so part of this trend may be inherited from that shift rather than real. This project has not tested how much.

source.dataset: MERRA-2 (Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2)
source.producer: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO)
source.access: NASA POWER Monthly and Annual API (NASA Langley Research Center)
source.kind: Reanalysis: a global model constrained by satellite and ground observations. Values are model-based estimates, not direct instrument readings.
source.caveat: MERRA-2 is a reanalysis: a model constrained by satellite and ground observations, not a direct measurement. Changes in the observing system over time (new satellites, fewer rain gauges) can create or hide trends, especially for precipitation and soil wetness. Check important results against an independent dataset.
source.credit: NASA GMAO MERRA-2 via NASA POWER
